comment: the-internet's Dynamic Controls: two buttons that each show a loading bar for a few seconds before the page changes (a checkbox is removed, a text field is enabled). Exercises WAIT after an asynchronous action, twice, undecided steps while a loader is visible (the runner waits them out with backoff and restarts the count when the page changes), and element_absent on the final page. The pass outcome carries no `requires`: the 'It's enabled!' check hovered at 0.79 while the outcome Choice read 0.81, and the exact facts are in `assert` anyway. The pass outcome names the button captions as well as the messages since the midday regression suite: on the finished page (both messages shown, 'Wait for it...' still in the text) the two-message wording read 0.77-0.82, on both sides of the 0.8 outcome gate, and two runs of three ended done_unverified with every assertion true.
goal: Click Remove and wait until the checkbox is gone, then click Enable and wait until the text field is enabled, so that the page shows both messages 'It's gone!' and 'It's enabled!' and the two buttons read Add and Disable.
notes: After each button a loading bar runs for a few seconds; the message appears when it finishes. Do not click the button again while the bar is running. The text 'Wait for it...' stays on the page after a loading bar has finished and does not mean anything is still loading: the finished state is the message under the section plus the button's new caption (Add after Remove, Disable after Enable).

checks.checkbox_gone: The message 'It's gone!' is shown and no checkbox is visible

both_done.when: The message 'It's gone!' is shown under Remove/add and the button there reads Add. The message 'It's enabled!' is shown under Enable/disable and the button there reads Disable

app_error.when: An error message or a blank page is shown instead of the Dynamic Controls example
